designs.title: Pisa
designs.why: Clean, confident one-ink line work that holds up at full size (no broken hairlines, the arcades and diamond inlays are crisp), and the 3.97° denomination is the tilt angle, a quiet joke a label can own. But at 3 m it reads as a gift-shop souvenir: an evenly weighted, outline-only tower with an empty white interior and a large blank sky makes it feel like clip-art rather than an engraved stamp. On white it is tidy and a bit thin; on black it becomes a white wireframe that actually looks more deliberate. The '3.97°' set big in the top corner can also be misread as a price tag. Nothing here gets it to $50 yet.
designs.fix: Turn the clip-art into an object: add a single-ink postmark cancellation (circular PISA date stamp plus wavy bars) running off the upper-right corner over the sky and the 3.97°. It fills the dead space, gives the mark wear and authenticity, and makes the angle read as a joke, not a price.
